title: SIU clears Toronto police officers who shot and killed man wanted in January homicide
subtitle: Ricardo Mirabelles, 37, of Toronto was shot by three officers five days after a 49-year-old woman was found dead in an apartment fire.
article: The Special Investigations Unit has cleared three Toronto police officers who shot and killed a 37-year-old man wanted in a Scarborough homicide earlier this year .
Emergency crews responded to a fire on Jan. 13 at around 3 a.m. at an 18-storey apartment building at 25 Bay Mills Boulevard , near Sheppard Avenue East and Warden Avenue.

Shortly after extinguishing the fire, 49-year-old Maryna Kudzianiuk was found suffering from serious injuries and transported to hospital where she died. An autopsy determined that her death was a homicide.

On Jan. 18, police attempted to arrest Ricardo Mirabelles, of Toronto, near Scarborough Town Centre in connection to her death. During his arrest, three officers fired their weapons and shot Mirabelles, who was taken to hospital and died from his injuries on Feb. 3.
There were "no reasonable grounds" to believe that any of the officers committed a criminal offence in the shooting, SIU director Joseph Martino said in a news release Friday.

According to the report, police attempted to pull Mirabelles over in his pickup truck. The SIU found that the man didn't cooperate with police in the arrest and was known days earlier for his involvement in the homicide and had a history of weapon offences.
Moments before the shooting, the man reached into his jacket, and officers feared he had a weapon, Martino said.

"Given the exigencies of the situation, and what in my view was the officers' reasonable concern that alerting the complainant of his arrest on a murder charge might further escalate the situation, I am not satisfied that the officers were in breach of their duty," Martino wrote in his report.
Martino said it doesn't appear the officers considered a stun gun a vaible option.

"Given the nature of the threat the officers reasonably believed the complainant represented, and the winter clothing the complainant was wearing that would have detracted from the weapon's ability to penetrate to the skin in order to immobilize the subject, I do not believe the failure of the officers to use a (stun gun) negates the reasonableness of their conduct," Martino wrote.

Kudzianiuk was the city's third homicide victim of the year. Family and friends described the 49-year-old as a "loving mother and an incredibly supportive friend" according to a GoFundMe campaign set up to cover funeral expenses.
"She was the nicest person I knew, really," said family friend, Alex Bedlitsky in a toronto.com interview earlier this year. "She was like a second mother to me."
